title: UPI Smashes Monthly Record With 23.66 Billion Transactions in July
excerpt: India's digital payments juggernaut set another all-time high, processing nearly 24 billion transactions in a single month as the platform expands to eight countries.
body:
• UPI processed 23.66 billion transactions in July 2026, a new all-time monthly record
  • The previous high was 23.20 billion in May 2026, meaning UPI has set records in three of the last four months
  • The platform now operates in eight countries and was cited by the US Congress as a model for digital payments
  • PhonePe and Google Pay's combined market share fell below 80% for the first time in May, signaling growing competition

India's Unified Payments Interface processed 23.66 billion transactions in July 2026, the National Payments Corporation of India confirmed, setting yet another monthly record for the world's largest real-time payments system. The figure surpasses the previous high of 23.20 billion set just two months earlier in May.

A System That Keeps Scaling

UPI has now set all-time records in three of the last four months, a pace of growth that continues to confound sceptics who predicted the platform would plateau. Daily transaction volumes averaged roughly 763 million in July, meaning Indians collectively made more than 31 million UPI payments every hour of every day.

For the full fiscal year 2025-26, UPI processed 24,162 crore transactions worth ₹314 lakh crore (approximately $3.7 trillion), cementing its position as the backbone of India's consumer economy. From street vendors to luxury retailers, UPI has become the default payment method for a country that was predominantly cash-driven just eight years ago.

Market Share Shifts

The duopoly at the top of the UPI ecosystem is showing its first cracks. PhonePe and Google Pay's combined market share dipped below 80% for the first time in May 2026, according to NPCI data, as newer entrants and bank-native apps carved out small but growing niches. WhatsApp Pay, CRED, and Paytm have all expanded their UPI user bases, while the Reserve Bank of India's interoperability mandates have made it easier for smaller players to compete.

The shift matters because regulators have long worried about concentration risk in a system that handles trillions of rupees monthly. A more distributed market is seen as healthier for the ecosystem's long-term resilience.

Going Global

UPI now operates in eight countries, including Singapore, the UAE, France, Sri Lanka, and Mauritius, with more integrations under discussion. The US Congress referenced UPI in recent hearings as an example of how a government-backed real-time payments system can leapfrog traditional banking infrastructure.

"UPI has demonstrated that a well-designed public digital infrastructure can achieve scale that private systems struggle to match."

— US Congressional Research Service report on digital payments

For the Indian diaspora, UPI's international expansion has practical implications. NRIs in Singapore and the UAE can already use UPI-linked apps for cross-border transfers and local payments, reducing dependence on expensive remittance corridors. NPCI International is actively negotiating with additional countries across Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Middle East.

What's Next

NPCI is working on UPI Lite X, an offline-capable variant designed for rural areas with poor connectivity, and UPI credit lines that would allow banks to offer instant small-ticket loans through the UPI interface. Both features could push transaction volumes even higher in the coming quarters, as the system extends deeper into underserved markets and new use cases.
nri_angle: UPI's global expansion to eight countries means NRIs can increasingly use the system abroad, while its record volumes underscore India's lead in real-time digital payments infrastructure.
author: Diaspora Desk
